A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ThinkEval/KnowGIC research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five editing techniques on Llama3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, a Harry Potter case study, and original-model knowledge diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on Llama3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and GPT2-XL, together with the retained case study and knowledge diagnostics.

M1.justification: The query-validation, CoT triplet-generation, human pruning/addition, and graph/chain-generation procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3, prompt templates, and the five-step chain cap match across versions; the streamlined overview diagram does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate factual editing through KnowGIC's MQuAKE-derived relational domains plus Harry Potter, using one- to five-step implication chains. Table 6 retains the same eleven base categories. More chains and an additional model change sampling and model settings, without establishing new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4 evaluate the same five techniques: AlphaEdit, MEMIT, RECT, PRUNE, and ROME. The Harry Potter comparison still uses AlphaEdit. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: KnowGIC expands from 558 to 1,406 chains, and evaluation adds GPT2-XL (1.5B) alongside the two retained models. Specificity is dropped from the reported evaluation metrics. Table 6 also changes the reported base-query templates from questions to completion stems.

E4.justification: Appendix A's diagnostic of pre-edit knowledge gaps loses Llama3-8B's 95% accuracy reference, while retaining Qwen2.5-7B's 81% and the same four prompt-failure examples. The 100-chain Harry Potter case study and its results are retained and relocated; no new ablation or robustness experiment is reported.

E5.justification: v1 Section 6 explicitly specifies a single run; v2 removes this disclosure without supplying a replacement run count. Both versions already describe five generations per case-study query, and neither reports confidence intervals or significance tests. The revision does not establish increased replication.

E6.justification: The main result matrix is extensively revised on the expanded benchmark: for example, Llama3 AlphaEdit's overall IFR changes from 0.5511 to 0.509. Five GPT2-XL rows are added, including AlphaEdit IFR 0.461, Preservation 0.663, and Efficacy 1.000. Specificity results are removed. These are results under revised settings, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The deductive-closure and deep-editing definitions, IFR formula, and CounterFact metric definitions are retained. v2's Preservation definition has the same formula and eligible-triplet set as v1's CKP. Renaming, attribution, and equation renumbering do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central framework, benchmark, and leakage-versus-preservation finding remain. v2 narrows metric novelty from two proposed metrics to IFR alone, adopting Preservation from prior work. It also explicitly presents deep editing as an evaluation setting supporting model and editing-technique selection.

C2.justification: v1's limitations concerning new-knowledge integration, direct-query evaluation, and one relationship per entity pair are removed, along with its model-bias ethics discussion. v2 Appendix B adds qualifications about graph incompleteness and human involvement. Section 6.3 additionally attributes GPT2-XL's poor preservation to knowledge entanglement associated with its smaller size.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports 83 relationship types, but Table 6 replaces v1's complete 21-base-triplet inventory with representative triplets. Prompts, pseudocode, and A100 80GB hardware information remain available. The actual dataset and implementation hyperlinks are unchanged, including links embedded in v1's references.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against RippleCoT, ChainEdit, UnKEBench, and ripple-effect and relational-editing benchmarks. New Appendix C and Table 5 compare unstructured, event-based, and deep-editing settings. Preservation is explicitly attributed to Cohen et al. rather than presented as the novel CKP metric.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around leakage and practical evaluation. ThinkEval now precedes Deep Editing; algorithms and the editing-techniques overview move into the main text, and the case study moves into performance evaluation. Dedicated limitations and ethics sections disappear.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Introductory figures are merged, the architecture diagram is redrawn, the case-study figure moves into the main text, and the result table gains color coding while plots expand to three models. The appendix's 21 knowledge-graph illustrations become eight retained examples; this does not establish removal of their underlying data.

improvement.justification: The third-model evaluation, clearer attribution of Preservation, and graph-incompleteness discussion strengthen evidence and positioning. However, v2 removes the single-run disclosure and important applicability limitations. Its revised discussion also incorrectly describes Qwen AlphaEdit's IFR as steadily increasing, although Table 4 falls from 0.579 to 0.497 between four and five steps. These gains and transparency/interpretation losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
